paper.title: A Fast Algorithm for the Real-Valued Combinatorial Pure Exploration of Multi-Armed Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Real-valued combinatorial pure exploration of multi-armed bandit (R-CPE-MAB)
unmapped: Learner pulls one of d base arms (standard-basis measurements) and observes that arm's R-sub-Gaussian reward, but must identify the best of K known real-valued action vectors in R^d (transductive linear bandit with standard-basis measurement set)
K is assumed polynomial in d
settings.definition_quote: Suppose we have $d$ arms ... We assume all reward distributions have $R$-sub-Gaussian tails for some known constant $R>0$. ... We define the action class $\mathcal{A} = \{\boldsymbol{\pi}^1, \ldots, \boldsymbol{\pi}^K\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ ... in each round $t$, she pulls an arm $p(t)\in[d]$ and observes a reward $r_{p(t)}$ ... find an action $\boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{out}}$ which satisfies $\Pr[\boldsymbol{\pi}^* = \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{out}}] \geq 1 - \delta$ as fast as possible.

tuning: confidence width beta_kl(t) = R sqrt(1/2 sum_s (pi^k_s - pi^l_s)^2/T_s(t) log(2K^2t^2/delta))

source.label: identification_accuracy
source.quote: The output of Algorithm \ref{OurAlgorithm} $\boldsymbol{\pi}^{a_{\mathrm{out}}}$ satisfies the following condition: $\Pr\left[\boldsymbol{\pi}^{*} = \boldsymbol{\pi}_{\mathrm{out}}\right] \geq 1 - \delta.$

results.notes: delta-correctness: misidentification probability at most delta. Compute is polynomial in K (enumerates the K actions).

symbols.V_s: max over pi in A with pi_s != pi*_s and pi' in A of |pi_s - pi'_s| / |pi*_s - pi_s|^2 * sum_u |pi_u - pi'_u|
symbols.Delta_s: Delta_(s): per-arm gap, extremum over pi != pi* of mu^T(pi* - pi)/|pi*_s - pi_s| (paper writes argmax; proof uses it as a lower bound, i.e. min)
symbols.A_ratio: A = max over s,u in [d], pi,pi' in A with pi_s != pi'_s of |pi_u - pi'_u|/|pi_s - pi'_s|
symbols.C_const: problem-dependent constant determined by R, {V_s}, {Delta_(s)}, A, d (and K, delta per proof)
symbols.sum_arms: sum over the d base arms s

conditions: R-sub-Gaussian rewards with known R (sigma = R)
any delta in (0,1), any action class A subset R^d, any mu in R^d

source.label: sample_complexity
source.quote: Assume any $\delta\in(0, 1)$, any action class $\mathcal{A}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, and any expected rewards $\boldsymbol{\mu}\in\mathbb{R}^d$ are given. The reward distribution $\phi_s$ for each arm $s\in[d]$ is an $R$-sub-Gaussian tail distribution. With probability at least $1 - \delta$, an upper bound of the sample complexity $\tau$ of Algorithm \ref{OurAlgorithm} is $8R^{2} \sum_{s = 1}^{d} \frac{V_{s}}{\Delta^{2}_{(s)}} \log ( \frac{2K^{2}C^{2}}{\delta} ) + Ad$ ...

results.notes: Sum is over the d base arms. C is an unspecified problem-dependent constant. Paper remarks that for ordinary d-armed BAI, V_s = 2 giving 16R^2 sum 1/Delta_(s)^2 log(1/delta).
